description: brief-14 DISPROOF (whole-matrix shifted-CQR3 + Ballard-LU as uniform n1024 path): MEASURED dead-end on the brief's own load-bearing test. Built a faithful PyTorch prototype (exact recipe, real reference.py n1024 inputs, FP64 gate; ran GPU-locked via autocuda run). WHAT WORKS: the Ballard reconstruction, derived+validated bit-exact vs geqrf -- V=strict-lower of UNPIVOTED LU of (Q-S), tau=-diag(U)/S, store triu(H)=S*R, S=-sign(diag Q); dense n1024 (kappa~1e5) PASSES the gate (factor 1.1e-3<1.2e-3, orth 1.3e-3<6.1e-3). WHAT FAILS (load-bearing): the shifted-CQR3 front-end on n1024 ILL-COND members. Kappa sweep pins the REAL validity at kappa(A)<=~1e5 -- at kappa>=1e6 the UNSHIFTED passes 2/3 hit a non-PD FP32 Gram and cholesky throws. The brief's premise 'n1024 worst kappa~1e5, 100x inside the 1.7e7 safe range' is FACTUALLY WRONG: it conflated the dense cond2 case (kappa~1e5, passes) with the stress members -- actual n1024 rankdef is kappa~6e301 (3n/4 columns EXACTLY ZERO), nearrank ~2.6e9, mixed ~1.7e12 = 1e4..1e296x beyond 1e5. Shifting ALL 3 passes avoids the crash but biases the factorization so far it FAILS the gate by ~1000x (factor 200-5000, orth 1.1-2.4) on every ill-cond case. geqrf passes all of them (factor ~5e-4, orth ~3e-5) so the GATE is satisfiable -- only CQR3 cannot. rankdef/nearrank are n1024 TEST shapes AND embedded in the n1024 MIXED benchmark shape, so a CQR3 n1024 dispatch FAILS local validate.sh. Per the brief's explicit kill criterion (report the failure, do NOT strip safeguards to force a pass), this is the honest verdict; the existing FP16-fast + per-matrix demote->geqrf hybrid is REQUIRED and stays. Doc-only commit 56a93c18 (code byte-identical to combine parent 1a1e7440; geomean 1738us, n2048-skip intact) banking the disproof + the validated Ballard recipe + the real kappa~1e5 boundary at the n1024 dispatch. SALVAGE NOTE: CQR3 IS valid+fast for the well-cond DENSE majority (kappa<=1e5); a CQR3-dense + geqrf-illcond per-matrix hybrid is the only viable variant, but that is what the current demote-routing already does in spirit (and the ill-cond fraction still needs the serial geqrf, so the '148-SM-fill' uniform-path pitch is unachievable).

brief-16 (CUDA-graph gap lever): DISPROVEN by a decisive cheap experiment + a clean loop simplification committed. The brief wanted a node-API CUDA-graph of the n1024/n2048 panel/trailing loop to recover brief-15's ~3% recurring per-launch gaps. TWO blockers found: (1) the trailing apply uses cuBLAS GEMMs (apply_block_reflector_t takes the cublasHandle; nvjet kernels in the profile) -- cuBLAS CANNOT be a node-API graph node, and stream-capture is banned, so a full-loop node-graph is INFEASIBLE; only custom-kernel fragments are graphable. (2) MORE IMPORTANTLY, the gaps are not host-recoverable. I ran the load-bearing test: HOISTED the per-inner-block cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) for PAF out of PAF_LAUNCH into the one-time init optin chain (cap want>=panel_pool>=apply smem; 5 live instances <8,1>/<8,2>/<32,{2,4,8}>), removing a redundant per-block host call (16x/call n1024). VERDICT: removing per-block host overhead was NEUTRAL => brief-15's ~2us gaps are NOT host-launch latency, they are GPU-side serial DATA-DEPENDENCY stalls (PAF ~85us/call vs ~5us host-launch, so host runs far ahead and never starves the GPU; the gap is PAF block N+1 waiting for block N's apply to write the trailing cols it reads). A node-API graph still respects those data deps, so it would NOT recover them either -> CUDA-graph lever DISPROVEN; the gaps are the irreducible serial-panel-chain latency. Building the graph = high-risk (wrong node param fails the gate, blast radius=the whole best loop) for a measured ~0% ceiling, so correctly not built. The hoist is kept (real clean simplification, gate-CLEAN, geomean-neutral). Committed d4e7299f. NOTE: parent is fcc6682d (_N2048_SKIP_DEMOTE=0); my brief-13 n2048-skip win is NOT on this branch -- a future combine should re-stack it.
